readiness_source: No entry here asserts that a fetch will succeed. Data access runs on the Kabo platform through data_connector_run; call data_connector_catalog for the authoritative connector ready / operation implemented state. The user configures no key, no CLI and no Python environment.

pp-youtube.runtime_note: Public YouTube evidence is fetched by the platform through data_connector_run; the platform holds the YouTube credential and the quota. This Skill owns the workflow and the evidence interpretation.

head-youtube-research.runtime_note: Outlier collection runs through tubelab-connector. The deep-analysis segment (gemini-video-adapter) is an optional add-on that is not implemented server-side yet: check data_connector_catalog, and when it is unavailable deliver the outliers and label the missing analysis as a platform-side gap. The Skill still enforces niche/channel consistency and a maximum of three deep analyses.

yt-reverse-viral-reels.runtime_note: Instagram public evidence is fetched by the platform, which also owns the credit ceiling. The Skill must keep every atomic response as evidence before cross-sample analysis and must not call provider endpoints ad hoc.

yt-youtube-research-agent.runtime_note: Public collection runs on the platform through public-video-media, whose three operations are asynchronous: a call returns a job rather than evidence, so treat evidence that has not arrived yet as pending, not as missing. Check data_connector_catalog first, because readiness varies by deployment - where the media execution host is absent the catalog reports ready false and calls answer unsupported, which is a platform-side condition the user cannot configure away. Say plainly which evidence is pending or unavailable and deliver only what the user's own inputs and other retrieved evidence support. Never present prior knowledge or web search as collected channel data.

yt-detect-creator-breakouts.runtime_note: Discovery runs on the platform; the dated snapshots stay local through creator-snapshot-store. A first run returns only recent_strong_performance, because growth ranking needs a later comparable snapshot.
